_notice: DEMO & SAMPLE DATA ONLY. This knowledge base provides illustrative reference data for CampusMate AI demonstrations. It does not represent verified official administrative policies, live institutional records, official deadlines, faculty office hours, or emergency dispatch services. Students must always confirm specific institutional requirements with their respective Dean of Student Affairs, Academic Department Office, or designated college authorities.

library_usage.borrowing_rules: Undergraduates can borrow up to 4 books for 14 days. Postgraduates can borrow up to 6 books for 30 days.
library_usage.renewals: Books can be renewed twice online if no hold has been placed by another student.
library_usage.fines_policy: Late returns incur standard nominal daily penalties. Overdue accounts cannot register for new semester courses until cleared.
library_usage.facilities: RFID self-checkout kiosks, quiet reading zones, photocopier and printing counter (Floor 1).
library_usage.etiquette: Strict silence in quiet zones; mobile phones must be silenced; no food or uncovered beverages allowed near library stacks.

safety_norms: Wear mandatory closed-toe shoes and safety coats/goggles where designated (Chemistry and Mechanical workshops)
Never operate high-voltage testing equipment or machine tools without the presence of the lab instructor or technician
Report damaged wiring, sparkings, or chemical spills immediately to the laboratory superintendent
Food, sugary drinks, and unsealed liquid containers are strictly forbidden around computer terminals and electronic breadboards
hardware_and_component_issue: Microcontroller kits (Arduino, ESP32, FPGA boards) require a valid student ID card deposit
Inspect all cables, probes, and components before signing out; report pre-existing damage to avoid liability
Return all components neatly back into component bins at least 10 minutes before the session ends
computing_lab_policies: Do not install unauthorized software or modify administrator configurations on lab PCs
Save your academic coursework to remote cloud repositories (GitHub, GitLab, or personal drive) as lab machines refresh nightly
Log off your workstation completely before leaving the laboratory

attendance_policy.standard_norm: A minimum of 75% attendance is standard across theory and laboratory courses to be eligible to appear for end-semester examinations.
attendance_policy.shortfall_procedure: If attendance drops between 65% and 75% due to valid medical reasons or representing the institute in technical/sports competitions, submit official medical certificates or representation letters to the Academic Dean within 7 days of returning to campus.
attendance_policy.critical_shortfall: Attendance below 65% generally leads to grade penalty or mandatory course repeat. Consult Faculty Advisor immediately.

medical_leave_submission.procedure: Visit the Campus Health Center for initial assessment. If treated off-campus, obtain a certified medical certificate and submit it alongside a formal leave application signed by your Faculty Advisor and HOD to the Academic Section.
medical_leave_submission.timeline: Application must be filed within 7 calendar days of resume date.

hall_ticket_and_exam_clearance.procedure: Download provisional admit card from the student ERP portal one week before examinations. Ensure library dues, hostel dues, and tuition fees are fully cleared.
hall_ticket_and_exam_clearance.mandatory_items: Physical student ID card and printed hall ticket are required for entry into every examination hall.

re_evaluation_and_grade_grievances.procedure: Grade grievances can be filed within 10 days of results declaration. Apply through the Examination Cell with receipt of the re-evaluation processing fee. Answer scripts are verified for re-totalling and un-evaluated questions.

health_center.hours: 24/7 emergency first-aid; Outpatient Doctor consultation 9:00 AM - 7:00 PM
health_center.services: Emergency medical stabilization, basic pharmacy, ambulance service, mental wellness counseling

cafeterias_and_dining.central_mess: Breakfast (7:30 - 9:30 AM), Lunch (12:00 - 2:00 PM), Snacks (4:30 - 6:00 PM), Dinner (7:30 - 9:30 PM)
cafeterias_and_dining.night_canteen: Open until 2:00 AM for study sustenance during exam weeks

sports_and_recreation.facilities: Indoor badminton courts, table tennis, gym/fitness center, basketball courts, athletics track
sports_and_recreation.gym_timings: 6:00 AM - 9:30 AM (Morning session) and 4:30 PM - 8:30 PM (Evening session)

campus_it_and_network_support.services: Campus Wi-Fi (802.1x) registration, institutional email credentials, VPN access for off-campus research papers
campus_it_and_network_support.reporting: Report network outages and router hardware issues via campus IT portal or direct help desk visit

common_student_questions.question: How should a first-year engineering student prepare for college?
common_student_questions.guidance: 1. Master foundational math and programming concepts early; they underpin upper-level coursework. 2. Attend orientation sessions to explore clubs and technical societies. 3. Form regular peer study groups. 4. Maintain a consistent sleep schedule and track assignments using a digital calendar. 5. Know your Faculty Advisor and department office location.

common_student_questions.question: What should I check if I have an attendance problem?
common_student_questions.guidance: 1. Check the official student ERP portal for verified attendance logs. 2. Calculate the exact number of classes needed to reach 75%. 3. If missed due to sickness, gather medical certificates and meet the course instructor during office hours. 4. Inform your Faculty Advisor early before the end-semester detention list is finalized.

common_student_questions.question: How can I prepare for practical examinations?
common_student_questions.guidance: 1. Ensure laboratory records and observation notebooks are verified and signed by instructors. 2. Review fundamental circuit diagrams, algorithm flowcharts, and code syntax. 3. Practice setting up experiments under timed constraints. 4. Prepare for the viva voce by reviewing the theoretical principles and potential sources of experimental error.

common_student_questions.question: How can I get started with technical clubs and hackathons?
common_student_questions.guidance: 1. Attend club freshman orientations in early semester. 2. Choose 1 or 2 clubs aligned with your interest (e.g., Coding or Robotics). 3. Build a small weekend project (e.g., a simple web app or Arduino robot). 4. Join a hackathon team with diverse skills (frontend, backend, design, pitch). 5. Focus on solving real-world student/campus problems.

common_student_questions.question: How should I approach a problem involving a campus facility?
common_student_questions.guidance: 1. Note specific details: exact room number, floor, building, and nature of the issue. 2. Check if the problem impacts safety or academic deadlines (e.g., lab Wi-Fi down before practicals). 3. Use the CampusFix mode to draft a clear, professional incident report. 4. Submit the report through your hostel warden, department IT helpdesk, or estate office.
